# Architecture Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that the architecture is specified with explicit boundaries, ownership, interfaces and change control.
**Created**: 2026-10-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [ADRs](../../../docs/adr/README.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Item tags**: `[Mandatory]` means the criterion derives from the constitution, an approved requirement, or an accepted ADR or ruling. `[Optional]` means it concerns an enhancement. `[Dnn]` refers to a detection from the checklist brief; the detection map is in [../gates/release-evidence-gates.md](../gates/release-evidence-gates.md). Post-implementation evidence checks are in that gates file, not here. Every item is unchecked, including `[Optional]` items, so `/speckit-implement` reports this file as incomplete until a reviewer marks it.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are application-plane and control-plane responsibilities documented, with a named owner for every runtime data store? [Completeness, Plan §1.3; ADR-004] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK002 Are all trust boundaries TB-1 to TB-6 defined with the controls applied at each? [Completeness, Plan §1.2; CON V] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK003 Is every external tool (git, scanners, subprocess, clock) required to be accessed through a named interface? [Completeness, CON VII; Plan §3.1] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK004 Are contract versions, owners and compatibility rules defined for every API and schema? [Completeness, Plan §2.2; contracts/README.md] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK005 Are change-control requirements defined for changes to architecture, schemas, security controls and workflow definitions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-GOV-009] [D14] [Mandatory]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is the allowed dependency direction between packages (api → domain → persistence; no domain types in `common/`) stated so a violation is detectable? [Clarity, ADR-004; CON VII] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK007 Is it specified which processes may write to which directories (runs write only under `var/`; never to `src/`, `tests/`, `specs/`, `docs/`)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-ORC-032, §FR-ORC-043; Plan §1.2 TB-5] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "the main working tree is never modified by a run" stated as a measurable criterion (byte-identical tree before and after)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-ORC-032; ADR-004] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the persistence isolation rule (one database file per shortener instance, one for the orchestrator) specified? [Clarity, ADR-002] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK010 Is horizontal scaling stated as documentation-only, with the single-instance components named (in-memory rate limiter, SQLite single writer)? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-SCL-002; Plan §8] [Mandatory]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Is every Complexity Tracking entry tied to a requirement that justifies it? [Traceability, Plan §Complexity Tracking; CON VII] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK012 Is an architecture-drift rule defined: which changes require a new or superseding ADR, and how drift between accepted ADRs and code is detected? [Gap, CON VII; Plan §9.4] [D25] [Mandatory]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are failure modes of the process topology (port in use, orphaned process, staging instance fails to start) specified with expected outcomes? [Coverage, ADR-004; Plan §6.2] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the minimum required for the AI-backed adapter (interface plus disabled stub) specified, so that deferring it cannot break other capabilities? [Clarity, Spec §FR-ORC-030; Spec §CST-008] [Optional]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- `[Gap]` = the requirement is missing; `[Ambiguity]` = the term or rule needs a definition; `[Conflict]` = two sources disagree; `[Assumption]` = relies on an unvalidated assumption
